sanskrit: yāvac cākṛtaviśvāsā drupade pārthivarṣabhe tāvad evādya te śakyā na śakyās tu tataḥ param
english: As long as Draupadī has not yet placed her full trust in Drupada, the bull among kings, for so long only are they now capable of being overpowered — not beyond that point.

sanskrit: eṣā mama matis tāta nigrahāya pravartate sādhu vā yadi vāsādhu kiṃ vā rādheya manyase
english: This is my counsel, dear friend, aimed at their suppression — whether it be right or wrong. But what do you think, O son of Rādhā?

sanskrit: karṇa uvāca duryodhana tava prajñā na samyag iti me matiḥ na hy upāyena te śakyāḥ pāṇḍavāḥ kurunandana
english: Karṇa said: Duryodhana, in my opinion your reasoning is not sound. The Pāṇḍavas cannot be subdued by stratagem, O joy of the Kuru line.

sanskrit: pūrvam eva hi te sūkṣmair upāyair yatitās tvayā nigrahītuṃ yadā vīra śakitā na tadā tvayā
english: Indeed, you tried previously to overpower them with subtle stratagems, O hero, yet even then you were not able to restrain them.

sanskrit: ihaiva vartamānās te samīpe tava pārthiva ajātapakṣāḥ śiśavaḥ śakitā naiva bādhitum
english: Even when they were right here, near you, O king, still children without fully-grown wings, you were simply unable to harm them.

sanskrit: jātapakṣā videśasthā vivṛddhāḥ sarvaśo 'dya te nopāyasādhyāḥ kaunteyā mamaiṣā matir acyuta
english: Now they are fully fledged, dwelling abroad, grown powerful in every way — the sons of Kuntī cannot be overcome by stratagem; this is my settled conviction, O Acyuta.

sanskrit: na ca te vyasanair yoktuṃ śakyā diṣṭakṛtā hi te śaṅkitāś cepsavaś caiva pitṛpaitāmahaṃ padam
english: Nor can they be ensnared in misfortune, for fate itself protects them; they are ever vigilant and they are earnestly seeking the throne of their fathers and forefathers.

sanskrit: paraspareṇa bhedaś ca nādhātuṃ teṣu śakyate ekasyāṃ ye ratāḥ patnyāṃ na bhidyante parasparam
english: Nor can dissension be sown among them, for those who are devoted to a single wife do not split against one another.

sanskrit: na cāpi kṛṣṇā śakyeta tebhyo bhedayituṃ paraiḥ paridyūnān vṛtavatī kim utādya mṛjāvataḥ
english: Nor indeed can Kṛṣṇā be separated from them by enemies — she chose them when they were reduced to destitution, so how much less now when they are resplendent with glory.

sanskrit: īpsitaś ca guṇaḥ strīṇām ekasyā bahubhartṛtā taṃ ca prāptavatī kṛṣṇā na sā bhedayituṃ sukham
english: The quality most desired by a lone woman — to have many husbands — Kṛṣṇā has obtained; she is therefore not easily divided from them.

sanskrit: āryavṛttaś ca pāñcālyo na sa rājā dhanapriyaḥ na saṃtyakṣyati kaunteyān rājyadānair api dhruvam
english: And the king of Pāñcāla is of noble conduct; he is no lover of mere wealth. He will certainly not abandon the sons of Kuntī even for the gift of a kingdom.

sanskrit: tathāsya putro guṇavān anuraktaś ca pāṇḍavān tasmān nopāyasādhyāṃs tān ahaṃ manye kathaṃ cana
english: Likewise his son is virtuous and deeply attached to the Pāṇḍavas. Therefore I hold that they cannot by any means be overcome by stratagem.

sanskrit: idaṃ tv adya kṣamaṃ kartum asmākaṃ puruṣarṣabha yāvan na kṛtamūlās te pāṇḍaveyā viśāṃ pate tāvat praharaṇīyās te rocatāṃ tava vikramaḥ
english: But this is what is now fitting for us to do, O bull among men, O lord of the earth: while the sons of Pāṇḍu have not yet struck deep roots, for so long they are to be struck — let your valour be exercised.

sanskrit: asmatpakṣo mahān yāvad yāvat pāñcālako laghuḥ tāvat praharaṇaṃ teṣāṃ kriyatāṃ mā vicāraya
english: As long as our side is great and the Pāñcāla force is weak, for so long let their destruction be carried out — do not hesitate.

sanskrit: vāhanāni prabhūtāni mitrāṇi bahulāni ca yāvan na teṣāṃ gāndhāre tāvad evāśu vikrama
english: As long as they have not yet gathered abundant mounts and numerous allies, O son of Gāndhārī, act swiftly and strike now.

sanskrit: yāvac ca rājā pāñcālyo nodyame kurute manaḥ saha putrair mahāvīryais tāvad evāśu vikrama
english: As long as the king of Pāñcāla, together with his sons of great valour, has not yet set his mind to exertion, strike swiftly now.

sanskrit: yāvann āyāti vārṣṇeyaḥ karṣan yādavavāhinīm rājyārthe pāṇḍaveyānāṃ tāvad evāśu vikrama
english: As long as Vārṣṇeya — Kṛṣṇa — has not yet arrived, drawing the Yādava host in support of the sons of Pāṇḍu's claim to the kingdom, strike swiftly now.

sanskrit: vasūni vividhān bhogān rājyam eva ca kevalam nātyājyam asti kṛṣṇasya pāṇḍavārthe mahīpate
english: Wealth, varied pleasures, and the kingdom itself — there is nothing that Kṛṣṇa would not abandon for the Pāṇḍavas' sake, O lord of the earth.

sanskrit: vikrameṇa mahī prāptā bharatena mahātmanā vikrameṇa ca lokāṃs trīñ jitavān pākaśāsanaḥ
english: By valour did the great-souled Bharata win this earth; by valour did Pākaśāsana — Indra — conquer all three worlds.

sanskrit: vikramaṃ ca praśaṃsanti kṣatriyasya viśāṃ pate svako hi dharmaḥ śūrāṇāṃ vikramaḥ pārthivarṣabha
english: Valour is celebrated as a kṣatriya's virtue, O lord of the earth; for valour is the inherent duty of heroes, O bull among kings.

sanskrit: te balena vayaṃ rājan mahatā caturaṅgiṇā pramathya drupadaṃ śīghram ānayāmeha pāṇḍavān
english: With our great four-limbed army, O king, let us quickly overpower Drupada and bring the Pāṇḍavas here.

sanskrit: na hi sāmnā na dānena na bhedena ca pāṇḍavāḥ śakyāḥ sādhayituṃ tasmād vikrameṇaiva tāñ jahi
english: For the Pāṇḍavas cannot be brought to submission by conciliation, nor by gifts, nor by sowing dissension; therefore vanquish them by valour alone.

sanskrit: tān vikrameṇa jitvemām akhilāṃ bhuṅkṣva medinīm nānyam atra prapaśyāmi kāryopāyaṃ janādhipa
english: Having conquered them by valour, enjoy this whole earth; I see no other means of accomplishing this end, O lord of men.

sanskrit: vaiśaṃpāyana uvāca śrutvā tu rādheyavaco dhṛtarāṣṭraḥ pratāpavān abhipūjya tataḥ paścād idaṃ vacanam abravīt
english: Vaiśaṃpāyana said: Having heard the speech of the son of Rādhā, the illustrious Dhṛtarāṣṭra, after honouring it, spoke these words in reply.

sanskrit: upapannaṃ mahāprājñe kṛtāstre sūtanandane tvayi vikramasaṃpannam idaṃ vacanam īdṛśam
english: Such a speech, filled with valour, is fitting for you, O greatly wise son of the charioteer, who is accomplished in weaponry.

sanskrit: bhūya eva tu bhīṣmaś ca droṇo vidura eva ca yuvāṃ ca kurutāṃ buddhiṃ bhaved yā naḥ sukhodayā
english: But let Bhīṣma, Droṇa, and Vidura, as well as the two of you, together form a counsel such as will bring happiness to us.

sanskrit: tata ānāyya tān sarvān mantriṇaḥ sumahāyaśāḥ dhṛtarāṣṭro mahārāja mantrayām āsa vai tadā
english: Then, having summoned all those counsellors, the greatly illustrious Dhṛtarāṣṭra, O great king, deliberated with them.

sanskrit: bhīṣma uvāca na rocate vigraho me pāṇḍuputraiḥ kathaṃ cana yathaiva dhṛtarāṣṭro me tathā pāṇḍur asaṃśayam
english: Bhīṣma said: A conflict with the sons of Pāṇḍu does not please me in any way. Just as Dhṛtarāṣṭra is to me, so without doubt is Pāṇḍu.

sanskrit: gāndhāryāś ca yathā putrās tathā kuntīsutā matāḥ yathā ca mama te rakṣyā dhṛtarāṣṭra tathā tava
english: Just as the sons of Gāndhārī, so too the sons of Kuntī are regarded by me; and as they are to be protected by me, O Dhṛtarāṣṭra, so likewise by you.

sanskrit: yathā ca mama rājñaś ca tathā duryodhanasya te tathā kurūṇāṃ sarveṣām anyeṣām api bhārata
english: Just as they are to me and to the king, so too to Duryodhana, and so to all the Kurus and to others as well, O descendant of Bharata.

sanskrit: evaṃ gate vigrahaṃ tair na rocaye; saṃdhāya vīrair dīyatām adya bhūmiḥ teṣām apīdaṃ prapitāmahānāṃ; rājyaṃ pituś caiva kurūttamānām
english: This being so, I do not favour conflict with them. Let peace be made with those heroes and the land be given to them today; this kingdom too belongs to their great-grandfathers and to their father among the foremost of Kurus.

sanskrit: duryodhana yathā rājyaṃ tvam idaṃ tāta paśyasi mama paitṛkam ity evaṃ te 'pi paśyanti pāṇḍavāḥ
english: Duryodhana, just as you, my dear, regard this kingdom as your patrimony, so likewise do the Pāṇḍavas regard it.

sanskrit: yadi rājyaṃ na te prāptāḥ pāṇḍaveyās tapasvinaḥ kuta eva tavāpīdaṃ bhāratasya ca kasya cit
english: If the suffering Pāṇḍavas have not received a kingdom, then whence would even you have a claim to it — or the lineage of Bharata, or anyone else?

sanskrit: atha dharmeṇa rājyaṃ tvaṃ prāptavān bharatarṣabha te 'pi rājyam anuprāptāḥ pūrvam eveti me matiḥ
english: But if you have obtained the kingdom by right, O bull of the Bhārata line, then they too had obtained the kingdom previously — this is my conviction.

sanskrit: madhureṇaiva rājyasya teṣām ardhaṃ pradīyatām etad dhi puruṣavyāghra hitaṃ sarvajanasya ca
english: Therefore, in friendliness alone, let half the kingdom be given to them; this is indeed for the good of all people, O tiger among men.

sanskrit: ato 'nyathā cet kriyate na hitaṃ no bhaviṣyati tavāpy akīrtiḥ sakalā bhaviṣyati na saṃśayaḥ
english: If it is done otherwise, it will not be for our good; and for you too, complete disgrace will certainly ensue — there is no doubt.

sanskrit: kīrtirakṣaṇam ātiṣṭha kīrtir hi paramaṃ balam naṣṭakīrter manuṣyasya jīvitaṃ hy aphalaṃ smṛtam
english: Hold fast to the protection of your reputation, for reputation is the highest strength; the life of a man who has lost his reputation is held to be fruitless.

sanskrit: yāvat kīrtir manuṣyasya na praṇaśyati kaurava tāvaj jīvati gāndhāre naṣṭakīrtis tu naśyati
english: As long as a man's reputation does not perish, O Kaurava, for so long he lives, O son of Gāndhārī; but one whose reputation is lost is truly dead.

sanskrit: tam imaṃ samupātiṣṭha dharmaṃ kurukulocitam anurūpaṃ mahābāho pūrveṣām ātmanaḥ kuru
english: Embrace this duty befitting the Kuru family, O mighty-armed one; act in accordance with your ancestors and with your own nature.

sanskrit: diṣṭyā dharanti te vīrā diṣṭyā jīvati sā pṛthā diṣṭyā purocanaḥ pāpo nasakāmo 'tyayaṃ gataḥ
english: By good fortune those heroes survive; by good fortune that Pṛthā lives; by good fortune that wicked Purocana, whose intent was their destruction, has met his end.

sanskrit: tadā prabhṛti gāndhāre na śaknomy abhivīkṣitum loke prāṇabhṛtāṃ kaṃ cic chrutvā kuntīṃ tathāgatām
english: Ever since that time, O son of Gāndhārī, I have been unable to look any living being in the face in this world, having heard that Kuntī was brought to such a condition.

sanskrit: na cāpi doṣeṇa tathā loko vaiti purocanam yathā tvāṃ puruṣavyāghra loko doṣeṇa gacchati
english: Nor does the world attribute that guilt to Purocana as it attributes guilt to you, O tiger among men.

sanskrit: tad idaṃ jīvitaṃ teṣāṃ tava kalmaṣanāśanam saṃmantavyaṃ mahārāja pāṇḍavānāṃ ca darśanam
english: Therefore this — their survival — and the sight of the Pāṇḍavas must be pondered as the means of washing away your sin, O great king.

sanskrit: na cāpi teṣāṃ vīrāṇāṃ jīvatāṃ kurunandana pitryo 'ṃśaḥ śakya ādātum api vajrabhṛtā svayam
english: Nor indeed can the paternal share of those living heroes be taken away, O joy of the Kurus — not even by the wielder of the thunderbolt himself.

sanskrit: te hi sarve sthitā dharme sarve caivaikacetasaḥ adharmeṇa nirastāś ca tulye rājye viśeṣataḥ
english: For they all stand firm in righteousness, all are of one mind, and they were driven out unjustly from a kingdom that was equally theirs.

sanskrit: yadi dharmas tvayā kāryo yadi kāryaṃ priyaṃ ca me kṣemaṃ ca yadi kartavyaṃ teṣām ardhaṃ pradīyatām
english: If you are to act according to dharma, if you wish to do what is dear to me, and if well-being is to be sought, then let half be given to them.

sanskrit: droṇa uvāca mantrāya samupānītair dhṛtarāṣṭrahitair nṛpa dharmyaṃ pathyaṃ yaśasyaṃ ca vācyam ity anuśuśrumaḥ
english: Droṇa said: I have heard, O king, that those summoned to counsel who are well-wishers of Dhṛtarāṣṭra should speak what is righteous, wholesome, and conducive to glory.

sanskrit: mamāpy eṣā matis tāta yā bhīṣmasya mahātmanaḥ saṃvibhajyās tu kaunteyā dharma eṣa sanātanaḥ
english: My counsel too, dear friend, is the same as that of the great-souled Bhīṣma: the sons of Kuntī must be given their share — this is the eternal law.

sanskrit: preṣyatāṃ drupadāyāśu naraḥ kaś cit priyaṃvadaḥ bahulaṃ ratnam ādāya teṣām arthāya bhārata
english: Let some pleasant-spoken man be sent at once to Drupada, bearing abundant jewels for their benefit, O descendant of Bharata.

sanskrit: mithaḥ kṛtyaṃ ca tasmai sa ādāya bahu gacchatu vṛddhiṃ ca paramāṃ brūyāt tatsaṃyogodbhavāṃ tathā
english: And let him go bearing much in the way of mutual gifts, and let him speak of the supreme advantage that would arise from that alliance.

sanskrit: saṃprīyamāṇaṃ tvāṃ brūyād rājan dūryodhanaṃ tathā asakṛd drupade caiva dhṛṣṭadyumne ca bhārata
english: Let him speak of you as greatly pleased, O king, and likewise of Duryodhana — repeatedly, to Drupada and to Dhṛṣṭadyumna as well, O descendant of Bharata.

sanskrit: ucitatvaṃ priyatvaṃ ca yogasyāpi ca varṇayet punaḥ punaś ca kaunteyān mādrīputrau ca sāntvayan
english: And let him describe the appropriateness and dearness of the union, and again and again let him speak reassuringly to the sons of Kuntī and the sons of Mādrī.

sanskrit: hiraṇmayāni śubhrāṇi bahūny ābharaṇāni ca vacanāt tava rājendra draupadyāḥ saṃprayacchatu
english: And let him present, on your word, O lord of kings, many bright golden ornaments to Draupadī.

sanskrit: tathā drupadaputrāṇāṃ sarveṣāṃ bharatarṣabha pāṇḍavānāṃ ca sarveṣāṃ kuntyā yuktāni yāni ca
english: And likewise to all the sons of Drupada, O bull of the Bhārata line, and to all the Pāṇḍavas, and to Kuntī — whatever is fitting for each.

sanskrit: evaṃ sāntvasamāyuktaṃ drupadaṃ pāṇḍavaiḥ saha uktvāthānantaraṃ brūyāt teṣām āgamanaṃ prati
english: Having thus spoken to Drupada and the Pāṇḍavas with words of conciliation, the envoy should thereafter address them regarding their return.

sanskrit: anujñāteṣu vīreṣu balaṃ gacchatu śobhanam duḥśāsano vikarṇaś ca pāṇḍavān ānayantv iha
english: When the heroes have given their consent, let a fine escort proceed; let Duḥśāsana and Vikarṇa bring the Pāṇḍavas here.

sanskrit: tatas te pārthivaśreṣṭha pūjyamānāḥ sadā tvayā prakṛtīnām anumate pade sthāsyanti paitṛke
english: Then they, O foremost of kings, constantly honoured by you and with the assent of the subjects, will abide in their paternal position.

sanskrit: evaṃ tava mahārāja teṣu putreṣu caiva ha vṛttam aupayikaṃ manye bhīṣmeṇa saha bhārata
english: Such conduct, O great king, toward them and your sons alike I consider appropriate — together with Bhīṣma's counsel, O descendant of Bharata.

sanskrit: karṇa uvāca yojitāv arthamānābhyāṃ sarvakāryeṣv anantarau na mantrayetāṃ tvacchreyaḥ kim adbhutataraṃ tataḥ
english: Karṇa said: These two, bound close by considerations of wealth and honour, second to none in every matter — that they do not deliberate for your benefit, what is more remarkable than this?

sanskrit: duṣṭena manasā yo vai pracchannenāntarātmanā brūyān niḥśreyasaṃ nāma kathaṃ kuryāt satāṃ matam
english: One who speaks of welfare but harbours a corrupt inner mind, concealing his true soul — how could such a person act in accordance with the counsel of the righteous?

sanskrit: na mitrāṇy arthakṛcchreṣu śreyase vetarāya vā vidhipūrvaṃ hi sarvasya duḥkhaṃ vā yadi vā sukham
english: Friends are not for welfare or the opposite in times of material difficulty; for by the law of fate, both sorrow and joy come to all in their proper course.

sanskrit: kṛtaprajño 'kṛtaprajño bālo vṛddhaś ca mānavaḥ sasahāyo 'sahāyaś ca sarvaṃ sarvatra vindati
english: Whether wise or unwise, whether young or old, whether attended by allies or alone — a man finds everything, everywhere, in its appointed time.

sanskrit: śrūyate hi purā kaś cid ambuvīca iti śrutaḥ āsīd rājagṛhe rājā māgadhānāṃ mahīkṣitām
english: For it is heard that long ago there was a certain king known as Ambuvīca, a ruler of the Māgadha lords, in Rājagṛha.

sanskrit: sa hīnaḥ karaṇaiḥ sarvair ucchvāsaparamo nṛpaḥ amātyasaṃsthaḥ kāryeṣu sarveṣv evābhavat tadā
english: He was bereft of all his faculties, that king, living by breathing alone; in all affairs he was wholly dependent on his ministers.

sanskrit: tasyāmātyo mahākarṇir babhūvaikeśvaraḥ purā sa labdhabalam ātmānaṃ manyamāno 'vamanyate
english: His minister Mahākarṇi became the sole master of power; thinking himself to have gained strength, he grew contemptuous.

sanskrit: sa rājña upabhogyāni striyo ratnadhanāni ca ādade sarvaśo mūḍha aiśvaryaṃ ca svayaṃ tadā
english: That fool then seized for himself the king's women, his gems and wealth — everything — and the sovereignty as well.

sanskrit: tad ādāya ca lubdhasya lābhāl lobho vyavardhata tathā hi sarvam ādāya rājyam asya jihīrṣati
english: And having taken that, greed from gain grew greater in the greedy man; having thus taken everything, he then desired to seize the kingdom itself.

sanskrit: hīnasya karaṇaiḥ sarvair ucchvāsaparamasya ca yatamāno 'pi tad rājyaṃ na śaśāketi naḥ śrutam
english: But though he strove, he could not seize that kingdom from the king who, though bereft of all his faculties and living by breathing alone, retained it — so we have heard.

sanskrit: kim anyad vihitān nūnaṃ tasya sā puruṣendratā yadi te vihitaṃ rājyaṃ bhaviṣyati viśāṃ pate
english: What else could account for that man's lordship but destiny? If the kingdom is destined for you, O lord of the earth, it will be yours.

sanskrit: miṣataḥ sarvalokasya sthāsyate tvayi tad dhruvam ato 'nyathā ced vihitaṃ yatamāno na lapsyase
english: Before the eyes of all the world it will certainly remain with you. But if destiny has willed otherwise, you will not obtain it even by striving.

sanskrit: evaṃ vidvann upādatsva mantriṇāṃ sādhv asādhutām duṣṭānāṃ caiva boddhavyam aduṣṭānāṃ ca bhāṣitam
english: Knowing this, discern the good and bad qualities of your ministers; the words of the corrupt and of the uncorrupt alike must be understood.

sanskrit: droṇa uvāca vidma te bhāvadoṣeṇa yadartham idam ucyate duṣṭaḥ pāṇḍavahetos tvaṃ doṣaṃ khyāpayase hi naḥ
english: Droṇa said: We know why you say this, driven by a fault in your own disposition. Corrupted by your enmity toward the Pāṇḍavas, you reveal our fault to us.

sanskrit: hitaṃ tu paramaṃ karṇa bravīmi kuruvardhanam atha tvaṃ manyase duṣṭaṃ brūhi yat paramaṃ hitam
english: But I speak what is supremely beneficial for the growth of the Kuru line, O Karṇa. If you think it is wrong, then speak what you consider supremely beneficial.

sanskrit: ato 'nyathā cet kriyate yad bravīmi paraṃ hitam kuravo vinaśiṣyanti nacireṇeti me matiḥ
english: If what I declare to be supremely beneficial is done otherwise, the Kurus will perish before long — this is my firm conviction.

sanskrit: vidura uvāca rājan niḥsaṃśayaṃ śreyo vācyas tvam asi bāndhavaiḥ na tv aśuśrūṣamāṇeṣu vākyaṃ saṃpratitiṣṭhati
english: Vidura said: O king, you must certainly be counselled by your kinsmen for your own good — but advice does not take hold in those who are unwilling to listen.

sanskrit: hitaṃ hi tava tad vākyam uktavān kurusattamaḥ bhīṣmaḥ śāṃtanavo rājan pratigṛhṇāsi tan na ca
english: That speech which Bhīṣma, son of Śaṃtanu, the best of Kurus, has spoken is indeed for your welfare, O king — and yet you do not accept it.

sanskrit: tathā droṇena bahudhā bhāṣitaṃ hitam uttamam tac ca rādhāsutaḥ karṇo manyate na hitaṃ tava
english: Likewise Droṇa has spoken at length what is supremely beneficial; and Karṇa, the son of Rādhā, holds that too as not being for your good.

sanskrit: cintayaṃś ca na paśyāmi rājaṃs tava suhṛttamam ābhyāṃ puruṣasiṃhābhyāṃ yo vā syāt prajñayādhikaḥ
english: And reflecting upon it, O king, I do not see among your true well-wishers anyone who could surpass these two lions among men in wisdom.

sanskrit: imau hi vṛddhau vayasā prajñayā ca śrutena ca samau ca tvayi rājendra teṣu pāṇḍusuteṣu ca
english: For these two are aged in years, in wisdom, and in learning; and they are equally disposed toward you, O lord of kings, and toward the sons of Pāṇḍu.

sanskrit: dharme cānavamau rājan satyatāyāṃ ca bhārata rāmād dāśaratheś caiva gayāc caiva na saṃśayaḥ
english: In righteousness and in truthfulness they are inferior to none, O king, O descendant of Bharata — not to Rāma the son of Daśaratha, not to Gaya — there is no doubt.
